newsitem.title: LEBANON: World Bank has "constructive" talks with Syria.
newsitem.headline: World Bank has "constructive" talks with Syria.

text.p: The World Bank has begun talks on resuming cooperation with Syria, which is seeking to restore relations with lender nations and institutions, World Bank President James Wolfensohn said.

Wolfensohn, who met Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus on Sunday morning, told a news conference in Beirut on Sunday night that their talks had been constructive and established a basis for further discussions.

"There will be further discussions and if and when we reach a solution, we'll be very glad. I would say in a very straightforward way I found our meeting very constructive and we'll continue to work with the government," he said.
It was the first visit by a World Bank president to Syria.
Wolfensohn travelled from Damascus to Beirut for talks on Sunday evening with Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and other Lebanese officials.

He said Assad and Syrian Finance Minister Khaled Mahayni told him that "Syria wants to resume its relations with a number of lenders around the world with whom there had been an interruption in terms of their payments and it was quite clear that they're doing such a job.
"They've already resumed their relationship with France, with Japan and with the EU (European Union) and they're in negotiations with Germany," Wolfensohn said.
He said International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus visited Assad in Damascus a couple of months ago.
"My visit was a continuation of that to try and see if there was some basis on which we also could act. We established a basis this morning for further discussions," Wolfensohn added.
